newsitem.title: POLAND: NFI units jump in surging turnovers.
newsitem.headline: NFI units jump in surging turnovers.

text.p: National Investment Fund (NFI) units in Poland's mass privatisation programme have been surging on institutional buying before the release of financial data of the scheme's firms in coming months, analysts said.
The units have jumped 17 percent to 102 zlotys since last Thursday's close, hitting a record turnover of 20.6 million zlotys on Thursday.

"Many investors think the units are currently undervalued and want to buy now expecting the data to prove good," said Wojciech Kossuth, an analyst at Bank Slaski brokerage, who expected further rises in price and turnover.
Analysts have said that as yet it is impossible to appraise the units sufficiently and that the presentation of firms' financial data will give investors a better clue.
The units started bourse trade on July 15 at 104 zlotys.

They have been on offer to Poland's 28 million adults since November at 20 zlotys apiece and will later be exchangeable for shares in each of the country's 15 National Investment Funds, grouping more than 500 firms undergoing privatisation.
So far more than 17 million NFI units have been sold on the primary market, with the certificates on offer until November 21 this year.
